import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

### Research Findings & Architectural Recommendations: Machine Load Transparency & Capacity UX I have conducted independent research on how machine load is calculated in SASE and how it is surfaced in the ACE TUI, focusing on the discrepancy observed in [`20261026_172751.png`](file:///home/bryan/tmp/screenshots/20261026_172751.png) (where the top status bar showed **6 running**, but the gauge read **`load: 3/8`**). The full research report has been written and registered as a durable artifact snapshot: - **Report Path:** [`machine_load_transparency_and_capacity_ux__gem.md`](file:///home/bryan/.local/state/sase/workspaces/sase-org/sase/sase_22/sase/repos/research/202610/machine_load_transparency_and_capacity_ux__gem.md) - **Artifact Label:** `research:202610/machine_load_transparency_and_capacity_ux__gem.md` (`file:explicit:c5f72437e8c7e4d87d73cf8c`) --- ### 1. Root Cause Analysis of the `load: 3/8` vs `6 running` Discrepancy The discrepancy is caused by a fundamental semantic difference between **Process Display Status Bucketing** and **Runner Capacity Admission Claims**, compounded by a core status-mapping flaw: ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph UI_Header["Status Line Header (Display Bucketing)"] H1["174 [6 running · 23 waiting · 145 done]"] H2["load: 3/8 (Runner Capacity Engine)"] end subgraph Active_Clans["Active Clans in @epic v1"] C1["bob-cli-ct: [R2 W1 D3] (folded)"] C2["sase-1oh.5.1: [R1 W4 D1] (folded)"] C3["sase-1oh.4.1: [R1 W2 D1] (folded)"] C4["sase-1oe: [R1 W2 D2] (folded)"] C5["sase-1n6: [R1 W1 D9] (folded)"] end subgraph The_6_Agents["The 6 'Running' Agents"] A1["bob-cli-ct.5 (Phase 5 Worker turn)
weight=1.0 · occupied=1.0"] A2["bob-cli-ct.3--mon (Phase 3 Monitor turn)
session: bob-cli-ct.3 · pid=None · occupied=0.0"] A3["sase-1oh.5.1.2 (Phase 2 Worker turn)
weight=1.0 · occupied=1.0"] A4["sase-1oh.4.1.2 (Phase 2 Worker turn)
weight=1.0 · occupied=1.0"] A5["sase-1oe.3--mon-1 (Phase 3 Verify Monitor)
session: sase-1oe.3 · occupied=1.0"] A6["sase-1n6.10--mon (Cutover Wait Monitor)
explicit queue_weight=0.0 · occupied=0.0"] end H1 --> Active_Clans C1 --> A1 & A2 C2 --> A3 C3 --> A4 C4 --> A5 C5 --> A6 A1 -->|Claim: 1.0| H2 A3 -->|Claim: 1.0| H2 A4 -->|Claim: 1.0| H2 A2 -.->|0.0: unverified pid| H2 A5 -.->|1.0: session claim / joined run| H2 A6 -.->|0.0: explicit w0 wait monitor| H2 ``` 1. **Who were the 6 "running" agents?** - **`bob-cli-ct`** (`[R2 W1 D3]`): `bob-cli-ct.5` (Wave 4 worker) + `bob-cli-ct.3--mon` (Wave 3 verify monitor). - **`sase-1oh.5.1`** (`[R1 W4 D1]`): `sase-1oh.5.1.2` (Wave 2 worker). - **`sase-1oh.4.1`** (`[R1 W2 D1]`): `sase-1oh.4.1.2` (Wave 2 worker). - **`sase-1oe`** (`[R1 W2 D2]`): `sase-1oe.3` / `sase-1oe.3--mon-1` (Wave 3 verify monitor running `sase tool run check`). - **`sase-1n6`** (`[R1 W1 D9]`): `sase-1n6.10` / `sase-1n6.10--mon` (Cutover gate wait monitor). - **Sum of in-flight counts:** `2 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 6`. 2. **Why `sase-1n6` counted as "Running":** In [`sase-core/crates/sase_core/src/agent_archive/status.rs`](file:///home/bryan/.local/state/sase/workspaces/sase-org/sase/sase_22/sase/repos/linked/sase-core/crates/sase_core/src/agent_archive/status.rs#L13-L30), `status_bucket_for_status` matches known statuses (`"WAITING"`, `"QUEUED"`, `"DONE"`). Any custom or compound status—such as `"WAITING CUTOVER"`—falls through to the default **`"Running"`**! This inflated the header count to 6 even though the monitor was passively waiting. 3. **Why the Rust Runner Capacity Engine computed 3.0 / 8.0:** Runner capacity tracks **active capacity claims against `max_running_agents` (8.0)**: - **`sase-1n6.10--mon`**: Holds **0.0 units** because it explicitly authored `queue_weight: 0.0`. - **`bob-cli-ct.3--mon`**: Holds **0.0 units** because its process handle was not registered with an active PID marker (under [`records.rs:is_occupying_record`](file:///home/bryan/.local/state/sase/workspaces/sase-org/sase/sase_22/sase/repos/linked/sase-core/crates/sase_core/src/runner_capacity/records.rs#L39-L47), monitors without live PIDs occupy 0). - **Serial Session Consolidation**: Multiple turns in a serial session (`agent_session`) share a single claim in [`claims.rs:build_claims`](file:///home/bryan/.local/state/sase/workspaces/sase-org/sase/sase_22/sase/repos/linked/sase-core/crates/sase_core/src/runner_capacity/claims.rs#L31-L86), with capacity equal to `max(weights)`. - **Active 1.0 unit workers**: `sase-1oh.5.1.2` (1.0), `sase-1oh.4.1.2` (1.0), and `bob-cli-ct.5` (1.0). - **Total:** `1.0 + 1.0 + 1.0 = 3.0 units`. --- ### 2. Critical Bug Discovered: Clashing "checkout / diff" Tooltip Labels In [`agent_load_indicator.py`](file:///home/bryan/.local/state/sase/workspaces/sase-org/sase/sase_22/src/sase/ace/tui/widgets/agent_load_indicator.py#L111-L127), the gauge has a tooltip intended to show: ```text Held by: • : ``` However, testing live against running processes revealed that every holder currently displays as: ```text Held by: • checkout: 1 • checkout: 1 • diff: 1 (monitor) • checkout: 0.25 ``` #### Cause In [`agent_runner_slots.py`](file:///home/bryan/.local/state/sase/workspaces/sase-org/sase/sase_22/src/sase/ace/tui/models/agent_runner_slots.py#L225-L228), `source_agent_by_artifact_dir` is built with a naive dictionary comprehension over `capacity_agents`. Because root agents and their workflow step child rows (`setup`, `checkout`, `main`, `diff`) share the same artifact directory, the step child rows **overwrite** the root agent row in the dictionary! The tooltip then extracts the child's `cl_name`, outputting `'checkout'` or `'diff'` instead of the real agent name. --- ### 3. Why the UI State is Currently Opaque 1. **Header Disconnect:** `6 running` (process count) vs `load: 3/8` (capacity units) gives no indication of whether "load" means CPU load average or slot usage. 2. **Hidden Weights:** Default weight `1.0` is suppressed by [`_queue_weight_badge.py`](file:///home/bryan/.local/state/sase/workspaces/sase-org/sase/sase_22/src/sase/ace/tui/widgets/_queue_weight_badge.py). Clan containers also suppress weight badges. When clans are folded, **zero weights or capacity figures are visible anywhere on screen**. 3. **Deck Panel Vacuum:** The Deck panel only shows a `QUEUE` section for agents waiting in the admission queue; once an agent is running or when a clan is selected, capacity information is entirely absent. --- ### 4. Recommended Solutions & UX Roadmap #### A. Fix the Capacity Holder Label Bug In [`src/sase/ace/tui/models/agent_runner_slots.py`](file:///home/bryan/.local/state/sase/workspaces/sase-org/sase/sase_22/src/sase/ace/tui/models/agent_runner_slots.py#L225-L228): Prioritize root agent rows over step child rows (`is_child_row=False`, `appears_as_agent=True`) when populating `source_agent_by_artifact_dir`. When fixed, holder tooltips immediately render true agent names (`sase-1oh.4.1.2`, `bob-cli-ct.5`, `research.5e.gem`). #### B. Fix Compound Status Bucketing in Rust Core In [`sase-core/crates/sase_core/src/agent_archive/status.rs`](file:///home/bryan/.local/state/sase/workspaces/sase-org/sase/sase_22/sase/repos/linked/sase-core/crates/sase_core/src/agent_archive/status.rs#L13-L30): Add a pattern matching `canonical_status.starts_with("WAITING") || canonical_status.starts_with("WAIT") => "Waiting"`. This prevents waiting monitors like `"WAITING CUTOVER"` from being bucketed as `"Running"`. #### C. Clan Container Capacity Rollup Badges In folded clan rows, display net capacity alongside process counts: - `bob-cli (RUNNING) x6 [R2 W1 D3] · 1.0 cap` - `sase (WAITING CUTOVER) x11 [R1 W1 D9] · 0 cap (wait monitor)` #### D. Runner Capacity Inspector Modal (`L`) Add an interactive modal bound to clicking the gauge or pressing `L`: - Shows machine limit (`8.0`), occupied units (`3.0`), and free headroom (`5.0`). - Tables active claims by real agent name, project, role, PID, and held weight. - Separately lists zero-weight monitors (`w0`) with explanations (e.g., `Wait monitor (%queue weight=0)`). - Lists queued waiters and admission blockers. #### E. Permanent Deck Panel Capacity Card Add a dedicated "Runner Capacity" card to the Deck panel for running agents and clans, detailing active claim lineage, authored `%queue` directives, and held weight.
